summary: Unexpected per-inference memory surcharge on batch embeddings invoice line
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports an unexpected 'per-inference memory surcharge' line on their March 8 invoice for a batch embedding job. The job was a scheduled batch embed run of 120k documents using rwd-embed-2.1; billing shows a separate memory surcharge line totaling $213.45 in addition to the expected batch-embed line item.

Impact:
- Customer received an unexpected charge (line item) that they do not recognize; total invoice increased by 10%.
- Finance team at BrightPath flagged the invoice and paused auto-pay pending explanation.
- Risk of customer dissatisfaction / churn for an enterprise-dedicated account.

Observed invoice details:
- Invoice ID: INV-2026-03-08-9981
- Invoice date: 2026-03-08
- Line items (excerpt):
  - batch-embeddings | rwd-embed-2.1 | 120k units | $1,921.05
  - per-inference memory surcharge | high-mem | 1,000 units | $213.45
  - total: $2,134.50

Expected behavior:
- Dedicated customers running scheduled batch embedding jobs should be billed according to batch-embed pricing (per-embedding/unit) and not receive a separate per-inference memory surcharge for the same work. Memory surcharges are intended for ad-hoc hosted/high-memory real-time requests where runtime memory allocation exceeds configured thresholds.

Customer request:
- Explanation for the surcharge and reversal/credit if it was applied in error.
- Confirmation that future scheduled batch runs will not incur this surcharge unless explicitly configured.

Additional context from customer:
- Job submitted via Dedicated job scheduler using API key key-prod-ded-01; timestamp 2026-03-07T22:47:12Z; job tagged with "monthly-client-embeds".
- Customer notes they recently switched model pinning from openembed-3b -> rwd-embed-2.1 on 2026-02-28 to reduce latency and expected costs.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer runs scheduled batch embedding using dedicated scheduler (job id: JOB-20260307-MB-88).
2) Batch creates N inference tasks with model rwd-embed-2.1 and metadata 'memory_hint': 'auto'.
3) Serving runtime records per-inference memory estimate >2GB for some microbatches due to a transient KV-cache population pattern.
4) Billing postback includes both a batch-embed aggregate record and a per-inference surcharge records from postback-processor.

- POST /billing/postback 2026-03-07T22:50:07Z body: {request_id: req-8b9f, surcharge: memory-high, est_mem_mb: 2450, units: 1} -> ack
- Billing reconciler: matched batch-embed aggregate; found 1x surcharge event that did not de-duplicate because rule 'surcharge-exclude-batch' returned false (rule cache TTL 15m)

investigation_notes:
Findings so far:
- Root cause: Billing rule 'surcharge-exclude-batch' is designed to ignore per-inference surcharge events when a batch-embed aggregate postback is present for the same job. A race condition exists when per-inference telemetry is emitted after the batch-aggregate postback but before the aggregator marks the job as 'completed' in the postback index. The rule cache TTL and ordering allowed one surcharge event to be accepted.
- Contributing factors: Recent change to serving telemetry (2026-02-27 commit ab12cd34) added est_mem to per-inference events for more accurate tooling. That telemetry caused billing to classify an event as "high-mem" for a 1s window.
- Scope: Initial scan shows ~6 accounts in prod last 30 days with similar pattern; 3 of those are dedicated customers.
- Temporary mitigation: Disabled automatic acceptance of per-inference surcharge events for dedicated batch jobs by adding an exclusion check in the postback-processor config (feature flag: disable-surcharge-for-dedicated-batch). This prevents new occurrences but does not retroactively remove past invoice lines.
resolution_notes:
Work in progress / interim resolution steps taken:
1) Provisional credit of $213.45 applied to BrightPath (CR-2026-03-BP-001) to unblock auto-pay. Customer notified.
2) Hotfix PR opened to enforce 'exclude per-inference surcharges when batch-aggregate exists for same job and customer_tier == dedicated'. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/789 (under review).
3) Billing team to re-run reconciler for invoices affected by this race window and issue adjustment credits where surcharge was incorrectly applied. Initial re-run queued and expected to finish by 2026-03-14.
4) Post-deploy monitoring: billing-analytics alert created to detect >0.5% of batch-embed invoices containing a per-inference surcharge for dedicated customers. Slack alert -> #billing-alerts.

Follow-ups / Actions:
- Deploy PR and confirm tests in staging (assignee: Eve Ramos). ETA merge: 2026-03-13.
- Run backfill/reconcile for 30-day window and create credits where applicable. Owner: Billing reconciler team. ETA complete: 2026-03-14.
- Update Confluence runbook to document this race condition and the 'disable-surcharge-for-dedicated-batch' flag. Owner: Jules Alvarez. ETA: 2026-03-16.
- Customer follow-up: Maya to confirm when credits are posted and close ticket upon customer acceptance.
